rationale: Recording the strongest consequence of the confirmed snapshot-ordering defect and the exact source that makes it reachable, without claiming it as an independent obligation. The ordering defect selects the first List entry, and the two consumers that take that entry are the leader's snapshot send and NewRaft's startup restore; reading the startup restore and the configuration scan together shows two distinct outcomes that follow from restoring a lower-index snapshot when the log store still holds a hole above it. No map change is proposed because the accepted objects already state the ordering defect and the recovery path.

feedback.answered: The ordering defect has two sourced consequences at startup, and they are consequences of the confirmed defect rather than separate obligations. First, restoreSnapshot tries the snapshots in List order and keeps the first that loads, setting lastApplied and lastSnapshot from it, so an inversely ordered retained pair makes the node adopt the lower-index snapshot: the applied state regresses relative to the newer snapshot the store holds until a leader re-supplies the missing range. Second, the configuration scan that follows in NewRaft starts at that restored snapshot index and walks up to the last log index calling GetLog for every index, panicking on a missing one; a hole in that range is exactly what a previous user restore leaves behind (that path burns the index above the last log and appends only above it), so restoring an older snapshot whose index sits below such a hole turns the ordering defect into a startup panic rather than a recoverable regression. The lower-index choice is what enables both outcomes: with the contract-conformant ordering the higher snapshot index would cover the hole.
remaining: Whether a node can legally hold the two ingredients together: a retained pair whose (term, index) are inversely ordered and a burned-index hole above the lower snapshot but below the higher one. The ordering half is confirmed; the coexistence with a user-restore hole is not.

Whether the startup scan reaches the hole before the pre-existing snapshot chain would be repaired by another path (a leader snapshot install arriving first, or the operator removing the older snapshot).
The tcp transport and pipeline pooling, the FSM batch manager and the testing helpers remain unread, as recorded previously.

Constructing that state would be the next discriminating step if the run continues, and it would extend the same responsibility rather than open a new one.
